item.title: 14-year-old Millie Pradawong uses AI and CRISPR to make microalgae produce more biofuel
item.description: Fourteen-year-old Millie Pradawong has developed an AI-powered computational tool that predicts how CRISPR gene editing could improve microalgae for biofuel production. Her project, MACRO, aims to increase oil production without reducing algae growth. A finalist in the 2026 3M Young Scientist Challenge, Millie hopes her work will support future research in clean energy and biotechnology.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: A well in Gujarat's Morbi has been shaking continuously with rippling water with experts having no clue why
item.description: In Morbi district of Gujarat, a well has been causing an unusual spectacle with its strange water oscillations since early August. Hundreds of inquisitive locals have flocked to Pranjivan Sadariya's fields to witness this rare occurrence. While local officials have dismissed seismic activity as a potential cause, initial investigations point towards groundwater recharge and trapped air as contributing factors.

item.title: Scientists release 42 snakes to bring a giant US species back
item.description: In Spring 2026, conservationists released 42 eastern indigo snakes into their historical habitats in Florida and Alabama. After a year of specialized care, these reptiles have adapted well, with monitoring indicating successful survival and breeding in the wild. This significant reintroduction effort seeks to restore self-sustaining populations of this unique snake species to their native regions.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: The 1900 mystery of three lighthouse keepers who vanished
item.description: In 1900, three seasoned lighthouse keepers mysteriously disappeared from Eilean Mor. When a supply vessel arrived, they found the lighthouse abandoned with signs indicating a hurried exit. Investigations uncovered no indications of violence or outside interference. The prevailing theory suggests a rogue wave may have taken the men by surprise. This enigmatic maritime case continues to baffle experts over a century later.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 1974, a German fisherman released thousands of baby catfish into a river; 50 years later they are threatening native wildlife
item.description: In 1974, German biologist Roland Lorkowsky introduced the Wels catfish to Spain's Ebro River, where they've since become a top predator, threatening native wildlife. Their large size and aggressive feeding present significant hurdles for conservationists trying to maintain balance. Worsening climate change conditions could facilitate their further invasion into European waters, leading experts to deem eradication efforts nearly impossible.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: 11-year-old boy took Abbot's kneecap in 1956; 70 yrs later, his widow returns it to the museum
item.description: A medieval abbot's kneecap and a floor tile have been returned to Glastonbury Abbey more than 70 years after they were taken by an 11-year-old schoolboy during an archaeological dig. The artefacts were kept in Australia for decades before the boy's widow brought them back following his death in 2025.

item.title: Trump angry over leak of US weapons shortage as Iran talks enter crucial phase: Report
item.description: President Trump expresses frustration over media claims regarding the depletion of US weapons stockpiles, fearing the leaks may undermine America's leverage in negotiations with Iran. While he admits some reports accurately reflect a tighter supply of advanced munitions, he aims to pursue severe penalties for those behind the information leaks. Vice President Vance characterizes negotiating with Iran as exceptionally challenging, referring to their people as radical.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Mishra

item.title: China's Taklamakan Desert is now capturing more carbon than it emits
item.description: China's shelterbelt initiative has made remarkable strides, turning arid desert borders into thriving carbon sinks. Through strategic vegetation choices, this project now captures more carbon dioxide than it expels. This achievement is anchored in mountain meltwater, vital for its irrigation systems. The initiative showcases the powerful impact of ecological restoration given optimal environmental conditions, though future water supply will be critical for sustaining these achievements.

item.title: Owens Faces Viral Backlash: X post alleges she walked back Bagley claims; debate over credibility grows
item.description: Candace Owens is facing fresh online criticism after a viral X post accused her of making inaccurate claims about Officer Bagley before later walking them back. The post questioned the credibility of her investigation and reignited debate over her reporting. A clip from Owens' show discussing newly reviewed footage also resurfaced, further fueling discussion as supporters defended her work while critics challenged the accuracy of her conclusions.

item.title: Prosecutors Outline Grim Allegations: Filings detail alleged planned killing; body reportedly hidden for months
item.description: Prosecutors have outlined new allegations in the murder case against singer d4vd, claiming a heated argument with 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez preceded her death in April 2025. Court filings allege the singer killed and later dismembered the teenager before concealing her remains in his Tesla. d4vd has pleaded not guilty to all charges, and his legal team maintains he neither killed Celeste nor caused her death.
